challenged_claim: In the hyperbolic-square theorem, genuine independence of the scalar hyperbolic variable from the projected pair can be replaced by a bounded conditional density of that scalar given the pair together with a bounded pair density.
correction: False. For any delta in (0,1), take independent Y~Unif(0,delta), Z~Unif(0,1/delta), U~Unif(0,1), and S=-Z^2/(2Y)+U. Then the full joint density of (S,Y,Z), the pair density of (Y,Z), and the conditional density of S|(Y,Z) are all bounded by 1, yet 2SY+Z^2=2YU has density (1/(2delta)) log(2delta/q) on 0<q<2delta, hence is unbounded at zero. This is not a QFORM counterexample because this correlated triple is not shown to arise as a linear image of an original-coordinate product law.
